For those considering switching from Windows to Mac, there are virtually no software limitations. Not only can the platform run all of the biggest PC applications, but there are countless useful applications that are exclusive to Mac.

The only major exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games run better on Mac than ever before, whether through official or unofficial means……

Apple has a dedicated game porting toolkit to help developers evaluate the performance of their Windows games on Mac, with the goal of encouraging and facilitating them to port their games to the Mac platform.

However, according to Filipe Esposito of Macworld, this toolkit has also been used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac. He is one of them himself, and stated that the latest beta version has brought significant performance improvements, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

I spent several days testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Pro, and found that the performance improvements fundamentally change the experience of running demanding Windows games…… Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, the same game settings, and the same benchmark, the frame rate of GTA V jumped from approximately 106 fps on GPTK 3 to approximately 176 fps on the GPTK 4 beta, an increase of about 66%. The game ran smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high settings.

He acknowledges that not every game will see such dramatic results, but he hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
